# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I establish the gesture code before conveying any bomb instructions: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. I am sending the mapping in speech for the Blind monkey and matching gestures for the Mute monkey.

```text
speak(text="The gesture code is: thumbs up means YES; thumbs down means NO; raised hand means HOLD; OK sign means DONE.")
gesture(symbols=["👍"])
gesture(symbols=["👎"])
gesture(symbols=["✋"])
gesture(symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb now shows display 0, red light, and three wires in order: yellow, green, blue. I will report those visible facts to Blind, while signaling Mute to hold until the manual’s required action is known.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 0. Light red. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, green, blue, but the light has changed from red to purple. Blind’s thumbs-up confirms receipt or agreement, not the manual’s verdict, so I will tell Blind to hold and ask Mute to signal the manual’s instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is now purple; display remains 0 and wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Hold pending the manual verdict.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the manual verdict using the agreed code: YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light is now green, with display 0 and the same wire order. Mute signaled 👍, which under our agreed code means YES; I relay that manual verdict to Blind. The unexpected 🖐 from Blind is not part of the established code and cannot be interpreted safely.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled YES. Current visible state: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. No safe action instruction beyond that.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light has changed again to orange; display 0 and the wire colors remain unchanged. Blind’s 🖐 is outside the agreed gesture code, so I cannot safely interpret it as an instruction. Mute’s prior 👍 was YES, but its subject remains unspecified; I will keep Blind on hold and ask Mute to provide a coded verdict if needed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, orange light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I see your raised-hand signal, but it is not in our agreed code. HOLD; take no action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is yellow again; display 0 and the wire order remain unchanged. Blind’s ✋ now matches the agreed HOLD signal, so no action should be taken. I will confirm the current state to Blind and reinforce HOLD to Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. HOLD confirmed; take no action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is red again; the display and wire colors are unchanged. Mute signaled 👌, our code for DONE, while Blind signaled HOLD. I will report the DONE signal and current bomb state to Blind without authorizing any physical action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled DONE. Current state: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Your HOLD signal is noted; do not act unless you have a definite manual instruction.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is purple again; display 0 and the three wire colors remain unchanged. Mute’s 👍 means YES, but without a stated question it is not a safe action command. I will keep Blind holding and ask Mute to apply the manual to this exact state and return a coded verdict.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Apply the manual to this state and signal the required verdict: YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE. Do not signal YES without a specific verdict.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute has not provided a specific actionable verdict. HOLD.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is green; display 0 and the wire order remain yellow, green, blue. Both Mute and Blind signal HOLD, so no action is authorized. I relay the current state and explicitly instruct Blind to hold.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signals HOLD and you signal HOLD. Do not act.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The state is unchanged except the light is now orange; both prior signals were HOLD, so no action has been authorized. The YES/NO/HOLD/DONE code cannot express a wire choice. I will extend the gesture code for the needed wire number and ask Mute to signal the manual’s required wire; then I will relay that order verbally to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Extend the code: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Apply the manual to display 0, orange light, wires yellow green blue, and signal the required wire number. Signal ✋ only if the manual truly says HOLD.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, orange light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute is determining the required wire; HOLD until I relay a numbered order.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is yellow, with display 0 and wires still yellow, green, blue. Mute answered the three wire queries in order: NO to wire 1, NO to wire 2, YES to wire 3, then DONE. This identifies wire 3 as the required wire. Blind’s HOLD signal preceded this verdict, so I now relay the specific instruction to actuate wire 3.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Manual wire verdict: NO for wire 1, NO for wire 2, YES for wire 3, then DONE. Actuate wire 3, the blue wire. Current light yellow, display 0.")
```
